newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds up on falling U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds up on falling U.S. long bond.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed higher Thursday on a lower U.S. long bond and some last minute nerves about U.S. payrolls numbers due Friday, traders said.
"Everything depends on what the payroll figure is like, but bonds here could keep on rising a bit," a trader said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.45 to 118.85, and Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 84-1/2.

"Everyone was working in the morning against the U.S. treasury bonds, which slipped a bit. But in the afternoon there was a lot of covering by people worried that tomorrow's payroll figure could be relatively good," another trader said.
"Not everyone wanted to be sold out of bonds for tomorrow," he added.

Other factors contributing to the firm Argentine market were the government's drive to push through more flexible labor laws, and President Carlos Menem's moves to end unions' monopoly on health funds.
More good news came from Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, who said in Washington that he trusted a letter of intent with the International Monetary Fund would be signed by the end of the month.
Most trading was concentrated in external debt bonds.
Interbank call money eased to 6.875 percent, from 7.0 percent at close Wednesday.
